error.signature: AI says giving your IRD number to your New Zealand bank is optional or only matters for large accounts
error.regex: (ird number.*(bank|account|optional)|new zealand.*bank account.*ird number|resident withholding tax.*new zealand|rwt.*non.declaration.*new zealand)

verdict.summary: New Zealand banks must withhold Resident Withholding Tax (RWT) from any interest a customer earns. Without an IRD number on file, the bank is required to apply the non-declaration rate of 45% to that interest, instead of a lower rate chosen once an IRD number is supplied. This applies from the first dollar of interest, not just to large balances.

dead_ends.action: Skip giving your IRD number to the bank because the account is small or you assume it only matters for filing an annual tax return
dead_ends.why_fails: Banks must apply the RWT non-declaration rate, currently 45%, to interest paid to any account without an IRD number recorded, regardless of balance size. This is markedly higher than the 33% default rate that applies once an IRD number is on file but no specific rate is chosen.
dead_ends.common_misconception: Newcomers assume an IRD number is only needed for filing taxes at year-end, not for how a bank withholds tax on everyday account interest from day one.

workarounds.action: Apply for an IRD number and give it to the bank at account opening or as soon as it arrives, choosing an RWT rate that matches your income
workarounds.how: Apply for an IRD number through ird.govt.nz (a bank statement or account-opening letter can serve as proof of address for the application). Provide the IRD number to the bank in person or via online banking, and select an RWT rate; this replaces the 45% non-declaration rate with a rate based on your income.
